note: Renville County park filling a wooded oxbow of the Mouse (Souris) River 15 mi west of Mohall: many seasonal and annual-lease sites with transient RV sites among them; boat ramp, fishing dock, playground, ball fields, chapel, and the Country Mouse bar and grill beside the convenience store. Office and check-in by the store, across the bridge. --Claude
summary: County page + 2026 rules + Firefly engine: $25/night (weekly/monthly/seasonal/annual posted, $3.50 reservation fee), online reservations via Firefly, walk-ins at vacant sites via caretaker; 20/30/50A electric, water from fill spigots only (stored water:true was derived and is wrong), no sewer, showers, dump, store. Riverfront physically supported; nightly status of the river sites unread (engine search captcha-gated).
flags: WATERFRONT (riverfront stored; physically supported, nightly sale unconfirmed): the Souris here is ~45-60 m wide (well over the 30 m creekside line). Imagery shows RVs on open grass 12-20 m from the water on the outer north bank (~48.7957,-101.7966, with docks) and 25-40 m from the water on the east side of the oxbow interior (three units ~48.7930,-101.7953 to 48.7934,-101.7951, plus one ~48.7947,-101.7958). The Firefly engine has a 'Waterfront' amenity filter and site classes 'Basic RV Site', 'Seasonal Lease', 'Annual Lease' and 'Gazebo', but its availability search runs only behind reCAPTCHA Enterprise, so no site number or nightly class could be tied to a river site. The north-bank cluster (sheds, decks, docks) looks seasonal. No official site map found. Reviewer call: keep riverfront only if a nightly 'Basic RV Site' is confirmed on the water; on the default-down rule it would be riverview.

HOOKUPS: the derived water:true is contradicted by the engine's own amenity 'Water Fill Spigots (No Site Hookups)'; written water:false. Electric raised 30 -> 50 from the engine's 50-amp filter (which sites carry it unread).

LONG-STAY: public county park, so the private-park five tests do not apply, but the posted seasonal ($2,000) and annual ($2,200) leases and seasonal-camper rules, and the HHS roster's 150 lots against the visible density, say most sites are leased. Nightly sites exist ($25 rate, 'Basic RV Site' class, 'transient campsites' named in the rules); their count is unread.
